## What this module is, and what it is not

`Frame` is a table as one typed array per column with a validity bitmap; every verb is
`(allocator, Frame, Spec) -> Frame`. It replaces `dataset` + `tabular` (the dataframe split
plan of 2026-11-05): the storage came from `dataset.Frame`, the verbs
from `tabular.frame`, and both stay in place until step R retires them.

**Not here, refused:** a row index or MultiIndex (pandas' index family, survey row 3: every
verb would carry its cost, and polars users do without — owner's decision 2026-11-05); a
lazy optimizer or SQL (row 78); chunked storage (79); Python-language mechanics (rows 6, 9,
14, 17, 22, 57); plotting and styling (72); Period dtype (70); Excel/SQL/pickle and other
client libraries (76). Arrow, Parquet and the other columnar formats (75) are separate
planned modules, `arrow` and `parquet`.

**Not here, by plan:** row verbs and `viaRows` (rule 3 of the plan: `Frame` is the only
table model, so the card measures the one path that exists); `dataset`'s private wire
(no rival, no public purpose).

## Design & invariants

**Storage follows the cells, not the declared `ColumnType`.** All cells of one `Value` tag
(or null) get that tag's array; a mix gets `.boxed`, a plain `[]Value`. A null cell holds 0
in its array and has its bit clear; NaN is a value in storage, but every verb counts it as
missing (pandas' `isna`). `storage_test.zig` checks, array by array, that `FrameBuilder`
and `columnFromCells` build exactly what `dataset.Frame.fromDataset` builds.

**A result borrows from its input.** A verb shares every column it did not touch, and a
selection of all rows in order shares the columns outright; temporaries stay in the arena.
**Hand-built frames** with arrays shorter than `len`, fewer `data` entries than `columns`, a
short bitmap or text offsets out of order read as null there, never past an array's end.

**The verbs run `tabular`'s code.** `core.zig` (accumulators, predicate, window
aggregates) and `keys.zig` (canonical key encoding, seeded factorizer with a work cap,
radix sort) are `tabular`'s, with their imports changed. Where a verb needs rows (a key
that is not one plain int or text column, `pivot`, the rank path of `sort`) it builds a
row view of the key columns only, so key equality and ordering are `Value.order`'s in every
verb. Row indexes are `u32`: a frame of 2^32 - 1 rows or more is `error.TooLarge`.

**Semantics are still `tabular`'s historical defaults** (`skip_na = false`, an int `sum` is
a float). The plan decides pandas and polars semantics as the defaults; that switch is a D2
item in § Backlog, made once the row verbs are no longer the oracle for it.

## Limits and refusals

The same constants as `tabular`, refused with `error.TooLarge` before the work is done:
`max_aggregate_cells` 2^24 (groups x aggregates), `max_unpivot_cells` 2^22,
`max_pivot_cells` 2^22 (row keys x column keys), `max_join_cells` 2^24 (output rows x
columns), `max_rolling_work` 2^30 element visits. Each is pinned by a test in
`src/verbs_test.zig` against the row verb's refusal. Hash tables refuse past their work cap
(`keys.zig`), so constructed keys end in `TooLarge`, not a hang.

## Verification

- `src/verbs_test.zig` — every verb against `tabular`'s row verb of the same name, 4000
  seeds per group of verbs over generated tables (12 column shapes, NaN, -0.0, nulls,
  mixed kinds), the same cells to the bit or the same error; hand-built frames; the caps.
- `src/oracle_test.zig` — all 1353 pandas/polars cases of `tabular`'s file, every one run;
  the known differences are listed in the file and must still differ.
- `src/more_test.zig` — `page`, `tail`, `topN`, `nlargest`, `sample`, `concatByName`,
  `partitionBy`, `valueCounts`, `describe`, `clip`, `replace`, `cut`, `joinAsof` against
  their row verbs, 4000 seeds each.
- `src/expr_window_test.zig` — `mutate`, `where`, `cast` over random expression trees and
  `window` over every operation with random parameters, per group or not, against
  `tabular`'s row verbs, 4000 seeds each.
- `src/storage_test.zig` — storage against `dataset.Frame`; `src/value_test.zig` — the cell
  model's own tests from `dataset` and a differential sweep against `dataset.Value`.

`dataset` and `tabular` are `test_deps` only (`zig build check-testonly`). When step R
retires them, `value_test`'s sweep and `verbs_test` lose their oracle; the frozen
vectors in `oracle_test.zig` do not.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class C · oracle n/a

- **Class C** — an internal data structure and verb library; no wire format others must agree with.
- **Oracle n/a** — class C/D carries no anchor debt.

**What the tests actually contain.** What pandas 3.1.0 and polars 2.1.0 answered, frozen
(`src/oracle_vectors.json`, filtered by `tools/filter_vectors.py` from `tabular`'s file,
which `modules/tabular/tools/oracle.py` wrote), and `tabular`'s row verbs as a re-derived
oracle on generated tables.

## Backlog / deferred

Plan steps: **D2** verbs (this list), **D3** input and output, **D4** speed, **D5** audit.
Row numbers are the D0 survey's.

**D2, the verbs `tabular` has as row verbs only** (move each against its row verb and the
vectors): `resample` (27) and ungrouped `reduce` (30; `aggregate` with an empty
`group_by` already gives it). Not moved, as compositions of the verbs here (survey §6):
`tabular`'s `weightedGroupSum`, `percentOfTotal`, `clampRange`, `outlierFlag`,
`mergeByKey`, `cumreturn`, `drawdown`, `rebase`, `forwardFill`, the `series` `expanding`/
`ewm`/`pctChange` (the `window` operations cover them); `datePart` waits for the `dt`
accessor (row 98); `format`/`formatColumn` for text rendering (row 77).
